method: Abstract records read directly (lida.sport-iat.de); 2019 review supersedes the 2016 volume-equated finding.

claims.claim: A review of 25 studies found that weekly frequency does not clearly change muscle growth when weekly sets are equal.
claims.source_title: How many times per week should a muscle be trained to maximize muscle hypertrophy? A systematic review and meta-analysis of studies examining the effects of resistance training frequency
claims.authors: Schoenfeld BJ, Grgic J, Krieger J
claims.finding: Volume-equated: no significant difference between frequencies; authors: strong evidence frequency does not meaningfully affect hypertrophy when volume is equated.

claims.claim: When frequency rose together with weekly sets, growth was slightly greater.
claims.finding: Significant effect favouring higher frequencies when volume was not equated; difference between 1 and 3+ days per week described as modest.

claims.claim: Context: an earlier 2016 meta-analysis (10 studies) favoured twice over once a week.
claims.source_title: Effects of Resistance Training Frequency on Measures of Muscle Hypertrophy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
claims.authors: Schoenfeld BJ, Ogborn D, Krieger JW
claims.finding: Twice weekly superior to once with volume equated (10 studies); superseded by the larger 2019 review, so the script follows 2019.
